newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian TV boss says Chechen leaders in hostage trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian TV boss says Chechen leaders in hostage trade.

text.p: The head of Russia's NTV commercial television channel, three of whose journalists were taken hostage in Chechnya, on Tuesday accused Chechen leaders of involvement in their capture.
Igor Malashenko told a news conference the only way they had been able to free the three, who returned to Moscow on Monday after 100 days in captivity, had been to pay a ransom.
He accused Chechen Vice President Vakha Arsanov of being directly involved in what he said was a hostage-taking business and suggested Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov must have known about it.

"Today I am completely sure that a widescale business has been established in the Chechen republic dedicated to hostage-taking and that the top leadership of Chechnya had a direct or indirect involvement in the captures," Malashenko said.

"We are sure that President Maskhadov, who visited Moscow yesterday, is at the very least aware of what is going on in his republic and...is either too weak and cannot help to free people or can and doesn't want to," he added.

Malashenko said he did not know whether President Boris Yeltsin, who hosted Maskhadov in the Kremlin on Monday for talks on relations between Russia and its breakaway republic, knew what was going on but urged him to take measures to stop it.
